reading.title: My family
reading.text: My name is Dilnoza. I am ten years old. I live in Samarkand with my mother, my father and my little brother. My brother's name is Azizbek. He is four. We have a cat. Its name is Mushuk. I love my family.

questions.q: How old is Dilnoza?
Who is Azizbek?
What is the cat's name?

reading.title: A day at school
reading.text: Tom gets up at seven o'clock. He has breakfast with his sister. He goes to school by bus. School starts at half past eight. In the morning he has English and maths. At twelve o'clock he has lunch. He goes home at three.

questions.q: How does Tom go to school?
When does school start?
What does Tom do at twelve o'clock?

reading.title: My room
reading.text: This is my room. It is small but nice. There is a bed next to the window. There is a desk and a chair near the door. On the desk there are some books and a lamp. I like reading in my room in the evening.

questions.q: Where is the bed?
What is on the desk?

reading.title: Food I like
reading.text: I like fruit. I eat an apple every morning. My favourite fruit is the banana. I don't like fish, but my sister likes it. For dinner we often have rice and chicken. We drink tea after dinner.

questions.q: What does the writer eat every morning?
Who likes fish?
What do they drink after dinner?

reading.title: A weekend trip
reading.text: Last Saturday, Madina and her friends took the train to a small town near the mountains. The journey took two hours. It was cloudy in the morning, but the sun came out at noon, so they had a picnic by the river. In the afternoon they walked to an old castle. Madina wanted to buy a postcard, but the shop was closed. They got home late and very tired, but they all agreed it was the best day of the month.

questions.q: How long was the train journey?
Why did Madina not buy a postcard?
How did the friends feel at the end of the day?

reading.title: A new reading room
reading.text: The city library has a new reading room for children. It is open from Monday to Saturday, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Children under seven must come with an adult. There are more than two thousand books, and on Saturdays at 11 a.m. a teacher reads a story. Membership is free, but you need your passport or school card to borrow books. Please be quiet and do not eat in the room.

questions.q: When can children listen to a story?
What do you need to borrow books?
Which thing is NOT allowed in the room?

reading.title: An email to a friend
reading.text: Hi Jasur, thanks for your message! I'm sorry I didn't write earlier. I was ill last week and stayed in bed for three days. Now I feel much better. On Friday I'm going to start a new English course. It's twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and the teacher is from England. Do you want to join me? We could go together after school. Let me know by Wednesday. Best wishes, Sardor

questions.q: Why didn't Sardor write earlier?
How often is the course?
What does Sardor want Jasur to do?

reading.title: Elephants
reading.text: Elephants are the largest animals that live on land. An adult elephant can weigh more than five thousand kilograms and eats up to 150 kilograms of food a day. Elephants live in groups, and the oldest female is usually the leader. They can talk to each other with low sounds that people cannot hear. Sadly, many elephants are in danger because people hunt them for their tusks.

questions.q: Who usually leads a group of elephants?
Why are many elephants in danger?
What is true about elephants' sounds?
options: People cannot hear some of them
They are the same as dogs' sounds

reading.title: Learning to cook
reading.text: When I moved to a new city for university, I could hardly boil an egg. Eating in restaurants was too expensive, so I decided to learn to cook. At first, my dinners were a disaster: I burnt the rice, and my soup tasted like water. Then my roommate, who works part-time in a café, showed me some simple recipes. Now I cook three or four times a week and even invite friends for dinner. Cooking has also helped me save money, because I spend about half of what I used to spend on food. The best thing, though, is that I enjoy it.

questions.q: Why did the writer start cooking?
options: To get a job in a café

questions.q: Who showed the writer some simple recipes?
How does the writer feel about cooking now?

reading.title: City bikes
reading.text: From 1 March, the city council is introducing a bike-sharing scheme. There will be forty bike stations across the centre, and the first thirty minutes of each ride are free. After that, the price is 2,000 sum for every 15 minutes. To use the bikes, you need to download the app and register with your phone number. Helmets are not provided, but the council recommends wearing one. Bikes must be returned to a station; if you leave one anywhere else, you will have to pay a fine of 50,000 sum. The scheme will operate every day from 6 a.m. until midnight.

questions.q: How much do you pay for a ride of 20 minutes?
What happens if you leave a bike away from a station?
Which statement is true?
options: You must register in the app
The bikes are available all night
The scheme starts in the summer

reading.title: A letter from a friend
reading.text: Dear Kamola, I hope you are well. We finally moved to our new flat last weekend, and it is a bit of a mess, with boxes everywhere! The flat is on the fifth floor, and luckily there is a lift, because my brother's piano was really heavy. I like the area: there is a park five minutes away and a small market where I bought fresh bread this morning. The only problem is the neighbours upstairs, who play loud music at night. I am going to talk to them politely this week. Please come and visit when everything is tidy. Love, Nigora

questions.q: What was really heavy?
What does Nigora like about the area?
What is Nigora going to do about the noise?

reading.title: Chess
reading.text: Chess is one of the oldest games in the world. Many historians believe it started in India about 1,500 years ago, and from there it travelled to Persia and then to Europe. In the past, only rich people played it, but today millions of people play online. Studies show that regular chess practice can improve memory and concentration, which is why many schools now teach it as a subject. However, experts also say that chess alone does not make you more intelligent: it is the thinking habits you develop that matter.

questions.q: Where did chess probably start?
Why do some schools teach chess?
options: It may improve memory and concentration

questions.q: What do experts say?
options: The thinking habits you develop are what matter
Only rich people can learn it

reading.title: Working from home
reading.text: Since the pandemic, remote working has moved from a rare perk to a mainstream option. Supporters argue that it saves commuting time and gives employees more control over their day. Yet the picture is more complicated. Several surveys suggest that people who work from home tend to put in longer hours, partly because the boundary between work and leisure fades. Managers, meanwhile, worry that spontaneous conversations, which often generate new ideas, are lost. Some companies have therefore adopted a hybrid model, asking staff to come to the office two or three days a week. Whether this compromise will last remains to be seen.

questions.q: According to the text, why might remote workers work longer hours?
options: They are paid by the hour
The line between work and free time becomes blurred

questions.q: What concern do managers have?
options: Informal talk that produces ideas is lost

questions.q: What does the writer say about the hybrid model?
options: It is a compromise whose future is uncertain
It is cheaper than remote work

reading.title: Bees in the city
reading.text: In recent years, rooftop beehives have appeared in cities from Paris to New York. Beekeepers point out that urban bees often do better than their rural cousins: cities offer a wide variety of flowering plants, and there are fewer pesticides than on intensive farms. But the trend has its critics. Some scientists warn that a large number of honeybees can compete for food with wild pollinators, such as bumblebees, which are already in decline. Their advice is to plant more flowers rather than to install more hives. Ironically, an initiative that was meant to help nature may, in some places, be harming it.

questions.q: Why can bees do well in cities?
options: There are many kinds of flowers and fewer pesticides

questions.q: What do some scientists fear?
options: Honeybees will take food from wild pollinators

questions.q: What is the irony the writer mentions?
options: A project to help nature may harm it
Wild bees are stronger than honeybees

reading.title: A letter of complaint
reading.text: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to complain about the laptop I bought from your online shop on 3 March (order number 4471). When it arrived, the screen had a visible crack, although the box was undamaged. I contacted your customer service twice, and on both occasions I was promised a call back within 24 hours, which never happened. Under these circumstances I would like a full refund. I am prepared to return the laptop at my own expense, but I expect you to confirm the refund in writing by 20 March. Otherwise, I shall have no choice but to contact the consumer protection agency. Yours faithfully, Dilshod Rakhimov

questions.q: What is the main problem with the laptop?
What does the writer want?
What will he do if he receives no answer by 20 March?

reading.title: Teenagers and sleep
reading.text: Teenagers are often described as lazy because they find it hard to get up in the morning. Research, however, suggests that the cause is biological: during adolescence the body's internal clock shifts, so teenagers naturally fall asleep later and need to wake up later. Unfortunately, most schools start early, which means many students are chronically short of sleep. A few schools in Britain and the United States have experimented with starting an hour later, and the results were encouraging: attendance improved and students reported feeling less anxious. Critics, however, point out that later starts create difficulties for parents who need to leave for work early.

questions.q: What does research say about teenagers' difficulty getting up?
What happened in the schools that started later?
What do critics say?
options: Later starts cause problems for working parents
